title: Vectors, Length and Matrices
mcqIntro: Twelve multiple-choice questions on Module 01. Work each one out on paper before choosing — several of them are designed so that the wrong answers are exactly what you get by taking a plausible shortcut.

mcq.stem: A drone has two programmed moves, $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}-2\\4\end{bmatrix}$. Which vector describes running the first move twice and reversing the second three times, that is $2\mathbf{v}-3\mathbf{w}$?
The sum of two vectors is $\begin{bmatrix}8\\2\end{bmatrix}$ and their difference $\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{w}$ is $\begin{bmatrix}2\\-4\end{bmatrix}$. Which one is $\mathbf{w}$?
For which pair does $c\mathbf{v}+d\mathbf{w}$ reach **only** a line through the origin, rather than the whole plane?

Two vectors $\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ span a plane through the origin, and you solve $c\mathbf{v}+d\mathbf{w}=\mathbf{b}$ by matching components. What role does the third component equation play?

options.a: It gives a third unknown, so all three can be found together.
options.b: It duplicates the other two, so it can safely be ignored.
options.c: It is a consistency test that $\mathbf{b}$ may fail, meaning no solution.
options.d: It fixes the scale of $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ before solving.

mcq.stem: Compute the dot product of $\begin{bmatrix}4\\-3\end{bmatrix}$ with $\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix}$. What is the result?
A student doubles the length of $\mathbf{v}$, leaving $\mathbf{w}$ alone. What happens to $\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{w}$ and to the angle $\theta$ between them?

options.a: The dot product doubles; the angle is unchanged.
options.b: The dot product doubles; the angle doubles too.
options.c: The dot product is unchanged; the angle halves.
options.d: The dot product stays the same, and so does the angle.

mcq.stem: Which statement is exactly what $\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$ tells you about two vectors?

options.a: They have the same length, whatever their directions.
options.b: They meet at a right angle, if neither is zero.
options.c: At least one of them must be the zero vector.
options.d: They are scalar multiples of one another.

mcq.stem: A plane $P$ through the origin consists of all $c\mathbf{v}+d\mathbf{w}$. You have checked $\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ and $\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$. Why is $\mathbf{n}$ perpendicular to every point of $P$?

options.a: Because two spanning vectors always fix a unique normal direction, up to length.
options.b: Because $\mathbf{n}$ can be rescaled to unit length without changing the plane $P$.
options.c: Because $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ are themselves perpendicular to one another.

mcq.stem: $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix and $\mathbf{x}$ is in $\mathbb{R}^2$. How many components does $A\mathbf{x}$ have?
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\0&3\end{bmatrix}$ act on the recipe $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\2\end{bmatrix}$. Which vector is the resulting combination of the columns of $A$?

short.prompt: Find scalars $c,d$ with $c\begin{bmatrix}2\\5\end{bmatrix}+d\begin{bmatrix}-1\\3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}9\\4\end{bmatrix}$. Show the expansion step, solve, and check your answer by substituting back. [3 marks]

Decide, **without solving for $c$ and $d$**, whether $c\begin{bmatrix}2\\6\end{bmatrix}+d\begin{bmatrix}-1\\-3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\5\end{bmatrix}$ has a solution. State the test you used and what it tells you about the reachable set. [3 marks]
Find the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}8\\15\end{bmatrix}$, and verify that your answer has length $1$. [2 marks]

This pair is HW 1-2 (2)(a). Find $\cos\theta$ for $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\2\\-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\\2\end{bmatrix}$, state $\theta$, and say what your answer means geometrically. [3 marks]

Show that the parallelogram with sides $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}6\\2\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\3\end{bmatrix}$ drawn from one corner is a rectangle, then verify $\|\mathbf{v}\|^2+\|\mathbf{w}\|^2 = \|\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}\|^2$ numerically. [3 marks]

Prove the parallelogram law $\|\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}\|^2+\|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{w}\|^2 = 2\|\mathbf{v}\|^2+2\|\mathbf{w}\|^2$ for arbitrary $\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w}$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Use $\|\mathbf{x}\|^2=\mathbf{x}\cdot\mathbf{x}$ and expand symbolically — do not choose specific numbers. [4 marks]

The vectors $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\0\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{bmatrix}$ span a plane $P$ through the origin. Verify that $\mathbf{n}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\-2\\1\end{bmatrix}$ is perpendicular to $P$, and explain in one line why checking two dot products is enough. [3 marks]

Compute $A\mathbf{x}$ for $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&2\\0&3&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}$ **both** ways — as a combination of the columns of $A$, and row by row. State how many components the result has and why. [3 marks]

Solve $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ for $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&0\\0&2&1\\1&0&3\end{bmatrix}$, $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\\14\end{bmatrix}$ using the row equations, then verify your solution with the column view. [4 marks]

Show that for any scalar $c$ and any vector $\mathbf{v}$, $\|c\mathbf{v}\| = |c|\,\|\mathbf{v}\|$, and explain where the absolute value comes from. Then use the result to explain why $\mathbf{v}/\|\mathbf{v}\|$ has length exactly $1$. [3 marks]

extended.title: A plane described two ways
extended.intro: This is **Midterm 2024, Problem II**, worked in full and on the paper's own vectors: the linear combinations of $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\-2\\1\end{bmatrix}$ fill a plane $P$ through the origin in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Parts (a), (b) and (d) are the exam's own four tasks in its order, walking from the 'combinations' description of $P$ to a single equation for it. Part (c) is not on the paper: it is added here because the consistency test it drills is the step most often skipped when a target has to be tested against a plane. Worked example 6 runs that test on a $\mathbf{b}$ that fails it; part (c) here runs it on one that passes, which is the case the notes do not work.

parts.prompt: Write the general point of $P$ as $c\mathbf{v}+d\mathbf{w}$, giving all three components in terms of $c$ and $d$. [2 marks]
Verify that the zero vector lies on $P$, and explain why this is automatic for any plane described as combinations of two vectors. [2 marks]

Determine whether $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\-2\\5\end{bmatrix}$ lies on $P$ by solving for $c$ and $d$. If it does, give the coefficients and say what the third component equation contributed. [3 marks]

The vector $\mathbf{n}=\begin{bmatrix}8\\8\\-8\end{bmatrix}$ is claimed to be normal to $P$. Test the claim, and if it holds, give the unit vector along $\mathbf{n}$ and the equation of $P$ in the form $n_1x_1+n_2x_2+n_3x_3=0$. [3 marks]

extended.title: A delivery robot with two step patterns
extended.intro: Parts (a) and (b) are HW 1-1 (3), with its own two vectors and its own target; parts (c) and (d) carry it further than the homework does. A warehouse robot executes only two pre-programmed steps, and may repeat or reverse either one any number of times (including fractional amounts, since the drive is continuous). Step P moves it $\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$ and Step Q moves it $\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}$, in metres east and north.

parts.prompt: Before computing anything, decide whether every point of the floor is reachable. State the arithmetic test you used and its outcome. [2 marks]
Find the numbers of Step P and Step Q that land the robot exactly at $\begin{bmatrix}14\\8\end{bmatrix}$, and check your answer. [3 marks]

The Step Q motor is reprogrammed so that Q now moves $\begin{bmatrix}2\\4\end{bmatrix}$. Show that the target $\begin{bmatrix}14\\8\end{bmatrix}$ is now unreachable, giving both the geometric reason and the algebraic contradiction. [3 marks]
With the reprogrammed Q, describe the complete set of reachable points, and give one target other than the origin that the robot can still reach. [2 marks]

extended.title: Two sensor directions
extended.intro: Two sensors on a mast point along $\mathbf{v}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{w}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-3\end{bmatrix}$ (metres, in a vertical plane). An engineer needs to know how they are oriented relative to each other and to a target direction.

parts.prompt: Compute $\|\mathbf{v}\|$, $\|\mathbf{w}\|$ and $\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{w}$, and state the angle between the two sensors, with the reason. [3 marks]
Give the unit vectors along $\mathbf{v}$ and along $\mathbf{w}$, and verify one of them has length $1$. [2 marks]

A third direction is $\mathbf{u}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix}$. Find the cosine of the angle between $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$, and say whether that angle is smaller or larger than the angle between $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$, justifying your answer from the signs. [3 marks]

Using $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ from this question, verify the Pythagorean identity $\|\mathbf{v}\|^2+\|\mathbf{w}\|^2=\|\mathbf{v}+\mathbf{w}\|^2$ numerically, and state the general result it illustrates together with its hypothesis. [2 marks]

extended.title: Altitudes, differences and an undo matrix
extended.intro: The matrix here is the $4\times4$ difference equation of HW 1-3 (2), which asks for $x_1,\dots,x_4$ and then for $A^{-1}$; the altitudes it is dressed in, and part (d), are this course's. A hiker records the change in her altitude each day, measured from a sea-level start: $b_1$ metres on day 1, $b_2$ on day 2, and so on. Her cumulative altitudes $x_1,\dots,x_4$ at the end of each day satisfy $x_1=b_1$, $x_2-x_1=b_2$, $x_3-x_2=b_3$, $x_4-x_3=b_4$.

parts.prompt: Write the four relations as a single matrix equation $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$, giving $A$ explicitly. [2 marks]
For $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}100\\50\\-30\\20\end{bmatrix}$, solve for $\mathbf{x}$ using the row equations, and verify the answer using the column view. [3 marks]
Read the pattern in your solution and write down the matrix $A^{-1}$ that turns any $\mathbf{b}$ back into $\mathbf{x}$. Describe in words what each of $A$ and $A^{-1}$ does. [3 marks]

A second hiker has $\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-2\\5\\1\end{bmatrix}$. Find her cumulative altitudes using $A^{-1}$, and check one component against the corresponding row equation of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$. [2 marks]
